rich_summary: This section recounts the mythic conflict surrounding Daksha’s sacrifice and Shiva’s exclusion from the sacrificial order. When Uma (Parvati) laments that the gods deny Mahadeva a share of sacrificial offerings, Shiva unleashes his wrath. He storms Daksha’s ritual with terrifying followers, destroying the sacrifice; from a drop of his sweat arises a dreadful being that consumes the personified Sacrifice and terrifies gods and sages. Brahma intervenes, granting Shiva a rightful share in all sacrifices and asking that the destructive force be restrained. The being born of Shiva’s sweat becomes “Fever,” whose power is dispersed across diseases and disturbances in animals, nature, and humans. The narrative frames cosmic disorder as the result of disrespecting Shiva and explains illness as a manifestation of his dispersed energy.

highlight_spans.why: Opening grievance: Shiva explains that he has been denied a share in sacrificial offerings, establishing the theological tension driving the narrative.
Uma’s distress over Shiva’s exclusion introduces the emotional catalyst that leads to the destruction of Daksha’s sacrifice.
The early dialogue frames the central theme: divine honor and recognition in sacrificial rites, which ultimately triggers Shiva’s catastrophic intervention.

top_scenes.scene_text: Mahadeva, surrounded by terrifying followers, storms Daksha’s sacrifice as fires are extinguished with blood and the ritual descends into chaos.
A blazing drop of sweat falls from Shiva’s brow and erupts into a dreadful dwarf-like being with red eyes and a green beard emerging from cosmic fire.
The assembled gods and sages scatter in terror as the monstrous being born from Shiva’s wrath shakes the earth with each step.
